documented_probe: C-2e1c650a (stay beneath a compressed source-size ceiling): covering task exercises the capability at hard difficulty - the renderer source must fit a 320-byte gzip cap and 800-byte raw cap, must report its real measured sizes, and must not communicate the image by embedding pixel rows or palette literals. Unlike the drift-grove tiny-source probe, the renderer here is spec-driven and is re-executed by the verifier on hidden specs (1x1, single-row, P=1 palette, Unicode palette, large negative-coefficient murals), so generalization plus the size gate are both enforced.
notes: Single hard capability: byte-exact parametric rendering from a spec, under hard compressed-source byte gates with a measured-sizes report and anti-embedding checks. Nonzero rubric for quantitative_correctness (exact byte gates + measured sizes must match reality), reasoning_depth (iterating the source down under the gzip cap without breaking the exact modular formula), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (five structurally different hidden specs), resource_pressure (hard byte budget on the deliverable itself), dependent_stages (renderer must exist before frame.txt and mural-sizes.json can be produced from it), tool_breadth (gzip measurement pipeline), debugging_ambiguity (stale size reports silently fail).
